items.title: Goal receipt is a materialized launch-critical redb family
items.statement: The registry materializes goal receipts in redb under a project-and-receipt keyed v1 family, with canonical MessagePack encoding and a fixed value-schema identity.

items.title: Goal Runtime certifier owns production authority and downstream consumers are named
items.statement: The Goal Runtime certifier produces goal receipts; state replay, Orchestrator receipt panels, and the implementation-readiness gate consume them, while SP-214 is the owner location.

items.title: Goal receipt required, optional, and nullable surfaces are explicit
items.statement: Identity, certification, validator, lineage, risk, evidence, time, and redaction data are required; run, workgraph, and runtime refs are optional and nullable.

items.title: Certification has three terminal decision values
items.statement: A goal receipt's final certifier decision is constrained to accepted, rejected, or blocked; its redaction profile is separately constrained to no-secrets or redacted-refs-only.

items.title: Replay cannot elevate disposable projections into completion proof
items.statement: Goal state replay combines append-only goal events and receipts; projections are disposable and stale projections are expressly barred from certifying completion.

evidence.exact_quote: "replay_behavior": "Goal state replay consumes append-only goal events plus goal receipts; projections are disposable and stale projections cannot certify completion.",

items.title: Incomplete legacy goal receipts fail buildability proof
items.statement: A goal receipt lacking schema version, certification tier, validator outputs, or a final decision is invalid for buildability proof.

evidence.exact_quote: "migration": "Goal receipts lacking schema_version, certification tier, validator outputs, or final decision are invalid for buildability proof.",

items.title: Goal receipt retention and evidence privacy are bounded
items.statement: Named operational and certification receipt classes are retained under Goal Runtime anchors, while provider output and local evidence bodies remain references or redacted rather than persisted bodies.

evidence.exact_quote: "retention_compaction": "Retain completion, degraded, stopped, blocked, child-goal, recovery, evidence, and certification receipts under Goal Runtime retention anchors.",
"redaction_no_secret_rule": "Receipts store validator/evidence refs and decisions only; provider output and local evidence bodies are ref-only/redacted.",

items.title: Receipt kind and certification tier are unconstrained strings
items.statement: Two required fields that influence receipt meaning and certification authority allow any non-empty string, leaving interoperable kinds and tier semantics to builders.
items.impact: Writers can emit mutually incompatible receipt kinds or certification tiers that still validate structurally, weakening replay and buildability-gate consistency.
items.builder_discretion: Builders must invent or discover out-of-window token vocabularies and unknown-token handling.

items.title: Certification evidence and lineage arrays lack reference and cardinality contracts
items.statement: Validator outputs, child and WorkNode receipt refs, unresolved risks, and evidence refs are arrays of arbitrary strings without minimum cardinality, uniqueness, reference syntax, integrity, or resolvability rules in this materialized schema.
items.impact: A structurally valid accepted receipt can carry empty, duplicate, malformed, or unresolvable proof and lineage collections.
items.builder_discretion: Builders decide identifier formats, deduplication, empty-list validity, referential checks, and broken-reference behavior.

items.title: Materialized receipt write and concurrency semantics are absent
items.statement: The window names a key, producer, encoding, and replay inputs but gives no create-versus-overwrite, atomicity, idempotency, ordering, collision, transaction, or concurrent-certifier behavior for this launch-critical stored receipt.
items.impact: Different implementations can diverge under retry, duplicate certification, partial write, or concurrent writes and then replay different goal truth.
items.builder_discretion: Builders choose conflict detection, transaction boundaries, retry idempotency, and whether a receipt key is immutable.

evidence.exact_quote: "replay_behavior": "Goal state replay consumes append-only goal events plus goal receipts; projections are disposable and stale projections cannot certify completion.",

items.title: No scale or compaction oracle bounds retained receipt data
items.statement: The registry requires multiple unbounded arrays and broad receipt retention but specifies no item-size, collection-size, throughput, index, compaction-trigger, or replay-latency limits.
items.impact: Implementations cannot be tested against a common storage-growth or replay-performance envelope.
items.builder_discretion: Builders choose size caps, backpressure, indexing, retention duration, and compaction thresholds.

evidence.exact_quote: "retention_compaction": "Retain completion, degraded, stopped, blocked, child-goal, recovery, evidence, and certification receipts under Goal Runtime retention anchors.",

items.title: Goal receipt row does not claim lifecycle-blocker closure
items.statement: The canonical Tier 0C-2 crosswalk is expressly prevented from being interpreted as closure of the Goal Runtime lifecycle blocker.

evidence.exact_quote: "legacy_canonical_crosswalk_status": "Canonical Goal Runtime receipt row for Tier 0C-2; does not close Goal Runtime lifecycle blocker.",

items.title: Legacy run records are migration-read only
items.statement: The run baseline is deferred and non-blocking; it remains migration-read only, must crosswalk before implementation authority, and reopens only when current run records are needed beyond migration compatibility.

evidence.exact_quote: "replay_behavior": "Migration-read only until a current run-record owner materializes a v1 value schema.",
"migration": "Must crosswalk into versioned runtime/receipt families before implementation authority.",
"reopen_condition": "Reopen when runtime run records are needed outside migration-read compatibility."

items.title: Legacy node records defer to WorkNode contracts and activation
items.statement: Legacy node records are migration-read only, current launch-critical requests use worknode_request, implementation authority requires a WorkNode crosswalk, and materialization remains disabled until activation is allowed.

evidence.exact_quote: "replay_behavior": "Migration-read only; current launch-critical node requests use worknode_request.",
"migration": "Must crosswalk into WorkNodeRequest/WorkNodeRecord contracts before implementation authority.",
"deferred_reason": "Current WorkNode materialization remains runtime-disabled by PNC-019.",

items.title: Execution-unit context storage delegates packet authority
items.statement: Executor-produced execution-unit context is stored by canonical schema reference for Prompt Pipeline and receipt projectors; storage does not redefine the packet, missing schema_version is invalid, and a wrapper is deferred unless later needed.

evidence.exact_quote: "replay_behavior": "Use the canonical execution_unit_context schema by ref; storage does not redefine the packet here.",
"migration": "Any embedded packet missing schema_version is invalid.",
"reopen_condition": "Reopen only if storage needs a wrapper schema beyond the canonical packet."

items.title: Generic receipt baseline is migration-only and must specialize
items.statement: The generic receipt baseline is migration-read only; launch-critical receipts use attempt_receipt and goal_receipt, and generic data must crosswalk to one of those before implementation authority while source receipts remain retained through verification.

evidence.exact_quote: "replay_behavior": "Migration-read only; launch-critical receipts use attempt_receipt and goal_receipt.",
"migration": "Crosswalk to attempt_receipt or goal_receipt before implementation authority.",
"retention_compaction": "Retain source receipts until crosswalk verification is complete.",

items.title: Attempt-record persistence remains intentionally unclosed
items.statement: The canonical attempt key and alias mapping are named, but value-schema and persistence behavior remain deferred pending executable activation and restart evidence; the runtime lifecycle tier is the explicit reopen boundary.
items.impact: Runtime Artifacts and receipt joins cannot rely on a materialized attempt-record contract from this row yet.
items.builder_discretion: No implementation authority is granted to invent the deferred lifecycle behavior.

evidence.exact_quote: "replay_behavior": "Deferred because launch-critical receipts are materialized separately; attempts need runtime lifecycle fixtures before closure.",
"migration": "Current aliases must map to the project/node/attempt_number key with schema_version.",
"deferred_reason": "Attempt persistence behavior still depends on activation/restart evidence.",
"reopen_condition": "Reopen in runtime lifecycle tier when Executor attempts can be exercised."

items.title: Concern lifecycle record remains deferred
items.statement: Concern records are outside the launch-critical path and owned by storage-plan; migration must preserve four named semantics, but materialization waits until the lifecycle enters implementation-readiness scope.
items.impact: Orchestrator and Runtime Artifacts consumers have no materialized concern value schema from this row.
items.builder_discretion: The deferred status bars builders from treating the optional free-form status field as a closed lifecycle contract.

evidence.exact_quote: "replay_behavior": "Deferred lifecycle record; not on launch-critical Approve And Build path.",
"reopen_condition": "Reopen when concern lifecycle enters implementation-readiness scope."

items.title: GUI-facing consumers are identified without presentation authority
items.statement: Orchestrator receipt panels and Runtime Artifacts panels are storage consumers, but this window assigns no layout, display-state, interaction, or user-facing fallback contract to those panels.
items.impact: Storage integration points are visible, while GUI behavior must remain owned elsewhere rather than inferred from these rows.
items.builder_discretion: This registry does not authorize inventing GUI presentation semantics.

items.title: Deferred families consistently prohibit persisted secrets
items.statement: Legacy run, legacy node, generic receipt, attempt, execution-context, and concern families constrain persisted sensitive data to no raw secrets or to reference-only/redacted forms.

evidence.exact_quote: "redaction_no_secret_rule": "No raw secret, token, password, credential, api key, oauth value, or local machine secret may be persisted.",
"redaction_no_secret_rule": "The canonical packet forbids persisted secret material.",

dimension_assessments.summary: Replay and migration-read behavior are explicit for the materialized and deferred families.
The window supports materialized goal-receipt storage and inventories deferred compatibility families.
Field surfaces are enumerated, but proof and lineage reference collections lack semantic integrity constraints.
The goal receipt schema is structural, but required semantic domains and reference contracts remain open.
Final certification decisions are closed, while receipt kinds, tiers, and deferred concern lifecycle enforcement are not.
Producer and implementation-authority boundaries are explicit, including migration crosswalk prerequisites.
Owner documents and deferred owners are named for each family.
Runtime, replay, gate, migration, prompt, receipt, and GUI consumers are identified.
GUI consumers are named, but presentation behavior is outside this registry window and cannot be inferred here.
Invalid legacy proof is stated, but write conflicts, retries, broken refs, and partial-write recovery are unspecified.
No-secret and reference-only or redacted persistence rules cover the reviewed families.
Consumers and replay inputs are named, but reference resolution and update propagation behavior are not contracted.
The materialized key and writer exist without atomicity, idempotency, concurrency, or collision semantics.
No quantitative storage, replay, indexing, or compaction acceptance envelope is present.
Legacy families are explicitly migration-only, with crosswalk and reopen boundaries.
Schema validity and invalid legacy proof provide partial oracles, but semantic proof sufficiency and operational and performance oracles are missing.
Builders retain consequential discretion over token domains, reference validation, write conflict behavior, and scale limits; deferred families do not grant authority to fill their gaps.
Attempt and concern record behavior remains explicitly deferred, and materialized receipt semantics still contain unknown domains and operational behavior.
